Title: More public awareness needed to stop spread of infectious diseases
NewsSummary: The Infection Control Society of Pakistan (ICSP), in collaboration with the Aga Khan University (AKU), held its Fourth International Conference on "Infection Control Challenges in the New Millennium," from November 23-24, 2000

content.text: The Infection Control Society of Pakistan (ICSP), in collaboration with the Aga Khan University (AKU), held its Fourth International Conference on "Infection Control Challenges in the New Millennium," from November 23-24, 2000. In his keynote address, Mr. John Templeton, Chief Executive, Craigvo Area Hospital, UK, emphasised that "A coherent strategy is required to address the problem. Antibiotics are not an excuse for bad practice. It is crucial that the dissemination of knowledge on disease prevention and control filters to the grass roots level."

The chief guest, Professor Mohammad Khurshid, Medical Director, Aga Khan University Hospital and Associate Dean Clinical Affairs, AKU, appreciated the efforts of the Society in creating awareness on infection control methods. He went on to encourage the Society to initiate training programmes in this field for health care personnel. Dr Hasan Nawab, President, ICSP, said that educational videos on topics such as hand washing and hepatitis as well as a health magazine, "Jahan-I-Sehat", were taking the lead in educating the public.

Amongst the other international speakers, Dr Paul Rooney, Consultant Microbiologist, Belfast City Hospital, Northern Island, noted the preventive aspects of T.B. He supported sputum tests for T.B diagnosis as the most cost effective, especially in diagnosing lung T.B that is a major source of the spread of infection. He also stressed the need to formulate a reliable local T.B prevention policy.

Dr Nizam Damani, Consultant Microbiologist and Medical Director, Craigvo Area Hospital, U.K, spoke on precautionary measures against the spread of infection in a hospital setting. He said that the use of brooms for sweeping hospital floors increases the bacterial count by 700 percent. He also advocated the use of disposable syringes for injections in all hospitals.

Dr Raymond Smego, Professor and Chairman, Department of Medicine, AKU, highlighted the prevention strategies for various blood borne diseases. Dr Wasim Jafri, associate Professor, Department of Medicine, AKU, focused on the prevention of Hepatitis Band C viruses as a major cause of chronic liver diseases in the country.
Prof Ali Muhammad Ansari, Professor of Orthopaedics and Ex-Director General Health, spoke on the risk of surgical infections and highlighted preventive aspects for reducing that risk.
